# CALYPSO

> Educational spacecraft cabin CO₂ simulation and sensor placement workbench.

## Project overview

CALYPSO models two air volumes: mixed cabin air and the air near an astronaut’s face. Users can adjust ventilation, CO₂ removal, and crew activity, inspect graphs, and reposition virtual sensors. The model is illustrative and does not provide medical or operational guidance.

## Reproduce the demo

1. In Simulation, select Start 60-second demo. The workbench computes 300 seconds of reduced-ventilation model output.
2. Reveal the modeled breathing zone. It first crosses the 1,250 ppm demonstration threshold at 36 seconds. The cabin sensor does not reach the threshold within the run.
3. Move S1 to the breathing zone. The same sensor detects the crossing at 36 seconds on the same model trajectory.
4. Download comparison data to inspect settings, samples, and detection results.

## Evidence and scope

The model uses two effective volumes with an illustrative local CO₂ source, symmetric exchange, and cabin removal. The 1,250 ppm threshold is an experiment rule. NASA Data displays measured RR-1 CO₂, temperature, and relative humidity for ISS flight and ground control separately from model results.

Crew Health is an optional NASA-linked body map under Extras; Crew Nutrition has been removed. Roger is an optional Gemini-powered guide to the model and NASA reference directory.

## Model transparency

The active model is a two-volume mass balance, not spatial airflow. A worker sweep covers 36 ventilation/activity settings under a fixed demo rule and exports its grid. NASA Data compares model cabin ranges with RR-1 context but does not calibrate or validate the model. An optional NASA reference requires a complete one-hour average and explicitly assumes 760 mmHg total pressure for conversion. Unverified mission limits are TODO. Roger is server-side, restricted by instructions to model/reference explanations, and marked AI-generated, may be inaccurate.
